African Cave Lodge, Hammanskraal: A Themed Retreat Near Dinokeng Game Reserve
African Cave Lodge is a 72-room property in Hammanskraal, 48 km north of Pretoria, built around artificial rock formations, cascading waterfalls, and cave-style architecture inspired by the mountains of Africa. Three lodges, four restaurants, four pools, a spa, and game drives to Dinokeng Game Reserve five minutes away make it a self-contained destination. If you are looking for something that feels genuinely different from a standard Gauteng hotel, this is it.
Location
The lodge sits just off the R101 north of Pretoria, easy to reach by car. Dinokeng Game Reserve is 4.4 km away — close enough to make a Big Five game drive a realistic morning activity. Temba City Shopping Complex is ten minutes by car, and Wonderboom Airport is 36 km away with a paid shuttle available on request.
The surrounding area is rural Gauteng rather than a tourist hub, so you come for the lodge and its activities rather than for what lies outside the gate.
Rooms
The three lodges offer different experiences. The Caves is the most distinctive — 20 rooms built into the artificial rock formations, including ten suites. The Heights is a two-storey building with balconies overlooking the pools and Big Five sculptures, with 35 rooms across standard and deluxe categories. Emzini Wezinsizwa has a more residential feel.
All rooms include air conditioning, flat-screen satellite television, fridge, minibar, free Wi-Fi, and a safe. Rooms are clean and well-maintained, and the cave-style interiors deliver the immersive atmosphere the concept promises.
Food and Drink
Five themed restaurants serve South African dishes alongside international and African cuisine, each with its own character. Three bars are spread across the property. The variety across the restaurants means you are unlikely to eat the same meal twice during a longer stay, and any of them can be privately booked for celebrations and functions.
Activities and Facilities
Game drives to Dinokeng, where you can see the Big Five, are the headline experience and bookable through the lodge. Traditional South African cultural dance performances cover all nine provinces with live drumming — worth making time for. A township tour with a stop at a local shebeen rounds out the cultural offer.
The spa covers massages and facials, four outdoor pools give you plenty of space to unwind, and there is a children s indoor play area for families. Ten conference rooms make the lodge a practical choice for corporate events.
Pros and Cons
✔ Genuinely distinctive cave and rock design — unlike anything else in Gauteng
✔ Five minutes from Dinokeng Game Reserve
✔ Five themed restaurants and three bars
✔ Traditional cultural dance performances and township tours
✔ Spa, four pools, and children s play area
✔ Free private parking
✘ Remote location — a car is essential
✘ Airport shuttle is paid rather than complimentary
✘ The themed design is immersive — not for those expecting a conventional hotel
Overall
African Cave Lodge is best approached as a destination in its own right rather than a base for exploring Gauteng. The game drives, the cultural performances, and the cave architecture give you more than enough reasons to stay put. Book a suite in The Caves, plan an evening around the dance show, and do the Dinokeng game drive first thing in the morning.
